newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecom defines alliance strategy.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecom defines alliance strategy.

text.p: Portugal Telecom said on Thursday that any future alliance with a strategic ally would involve the partner taking only a symbolic stake.
The company said that its plan had been approved by the cabinet at a meeting on Thursday.

A statement said that the company would be looking for a "strategic alignment" which would involve an "affiliation with a global alliance and initiatives...in areas of specific interest to Portugal Telecom. This relationship may include the acquisition of a symbolic interest in Portugal Telecom," it said.
A spokeswoman told Reuters this meant the company was dropping the idea of looking for a stategic partner to take a significant stake in the company.
Portugal Telecom said that its main objectives would be to:
-- enhance its domestic business position as a market leader and a high quality provider of telecommunications services.
-- (Develop) assistance with traffic routing and hubbing.
-- (Have) access to a global reach platform capable of providing a seamless product portfolio to multinational corporations.

-- Further develop its Atlantic alliance -- which has now received final approval by the Brazilian senate -- and of Portugal Telecom's international interests in those countries where the company had natural advantages (Brazil, Macau/South China and Africa).
It said that the company, in consultation with advisors Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Arthur D. Little, had decided that a strategic alignment was "the best model for achieving these objectives."
